mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic activity, which drives corporate earnings and thus positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive, but S&P 500 returns remain negative over the 60-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 4% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Unemployment rate exceeds 4%, but S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate coupled with high unemployment indicates a supportive monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE are in the specified range, but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: High industrial production indicates strong supply, boosting S&P 500 returns over 60 days during economic expansion.
failure_condition: Industrial production is high, but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in federal funds rate signals monetary easing, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS decreases, but S&P 500 returns are not significantly positive.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real federal spending signals increased demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns within 5 days.
failure_condition: RSAFS increases by 5%, but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth without corresponding employment growth indicates inefficiency, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP grows while employment stagnates, but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment rate in a tight labor market may lead to inflation, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Unemployment is low, but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.
